summary_paragraph: A man with a history of type 2 diabetes, end-stage renal disease status post kidney transplant, peripheral vascular disease, and obstructive sleep apnea was admitted for worsening chronic back pain and abdominal discomfort. His back pain, described as a constant burning sensation in the mid-thoracic region, was evaluated with imaging including a chest MRA and thoracic spine X-ray, both of which showed no acute abnormalities. The pain was deemed likely musculoskeletal, and his pain regimen was optimized with increased acetaminophen and addition of tizanidine. Abdominal bloating and pain were attributed to newly diagnosed pancreatic insufficiency, confirmed by stool testing, and he was started on Creon. His kidney function remained stable, immunosuppressive and chronic disease medications were continued, and he was discharged home with follow-up arranged with his primary care provider and gastroenterologist.
